Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that being a new mother can be a life-changing experience, filled with emotions, challenges, and joys. It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed, and that's why I'm here to support you.

As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and identify any potential concerns related to your postpartum experience. The purpose of this assessment is to provide a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and emotions, and to help us work together to ensure you're receiving the care and support you need during this time.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential, and I'm here to listen without judgment. My goal is to create a comfortable and non-threatening environment where you feel free to express yourself honestly. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us better understand your emotional well-being over the past week. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll be here to support you throughout our conversation.

Let's get started. I want to begin by asking: Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still find some things funny, like my baby's little facial expressions, but it's just not the same as before. I feel like I've lost a bit of my sense of humor, and things that used to make me laugh just don't seem as funny anymore. Sometimes I'll be playing with my baby, and I'll think, "Oh, this is cute," but it's not like I'm really laughing or feeling the joy that I used to. It's like everything feels a bit more serious and overwhelming now. Even when my husband tries to make me laugh, it's just not the same. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? (sighs) Does that make sense?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(sighs) Yeah, like I said, not really. I mean, I can appreciate when something is funny, but it's just not the same. I don't feel like I'm really laughing or enjoying things like I used to. It's like, I'll be watching a funny video or something, and I'll think, "Oh, yeah, that's funny," but I won't actually laugh. Or, if I do laugh, it's just a little bit, and it doesn't feel as genuine as it used to. It's hard to explain. I just feel like I'm missing out on the joy and happiness that I used to feel, you know? (pauses, looking down) And it's not just laughing, it's just... everything feels so much harder now. Taking care of the baby, doing chores, even just getting out of bed in the morning... it all just feels so overwhelming. (looks up, eyes welling up with tears) Sorry, I don't know why I'm getting emotional. It's just... being a mom is hard, and I feel like I'm not doing it very well.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shakes head) Not really. I mean, I used to love doing things like going for walks, reading books, or meeting up with friends. But now, it all just feels like so much effort. Even things that I used to enjoy, like spending time with my baby, feel overwhelming sometimes. I love my baby, of course, but it's just... everything feels so different now. I don't really feel like doing much of anything, to be honest. (pauses, looking down) I've been trying to get out of the house more, just to get some fresh air and stuff, but even that feels like a chore. And when I do try to do something I used to enjoy, it's just not the same. I'll be like, "Oh, I'm going to go for a walk," and then I'll get halfway through it and just feel so tired and overwhelmed that I'll just want to go back home. (sighs) It's like, I've lost my motivation or something. I just don't feel like doing anything anymore, and that's really scary for me because I used to be such a active and enthusiastic person. (looks up, eyes welling up with tears) Sorry, it's just really hard for me to explain.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nods, looking down) Yeah, that sounds like me. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If the baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If I'm tired, I think it's because I'm not managing my time well enough. If my husband is stressed, I think it's because I'm not supporting him enough. (sighs) It's like, I just feel like I'm not doing anything right, and that everything is my fault. Even when my husband tries to reassure me, I just can't shake the feeling that I'm failing somehow. (pauses, looking up) And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, if I forget to do something, or if I don't get the laundry done on time, I'll just beat myself up over it. I'll think, "Why can't I just get it together? Why can't I be a better mom?" (shakes head) It's just really hard for me to be kind to myself right now. I feel like I'm just making mistake after mistake, and that I'm not good enough. (looks down, voice cracking) Sorry, it's just really hard for me to talk about this.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nods, taking a deep breath) Oh, yeah. That's me all the time now. I worry about everything. Is the baby eating enough? Is the baby sleeping enough? Is the baby safe? (pauses, looking anxious) I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and suddenly I'll think, "What if I'm not doing this right? What if the baby is allergic to something?" Or, I'll be putting the baby to sleep, and I'll think, "What if the baby stops breathing? What if something happens to the baby while I'm sleeping?" (shakes head) It's like, my mind just won't stop. I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll just be going over all these worst-case scenarios in my head. (sighs) And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I'll worry about my husband, about our relationship, about our finances... (trails off) It's just, I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. (looks up, eyes wide with anxiety) And the worst part is, I know it's not rational. I know that most of the time, everything is fine. But my brain just won't listen. It's like, it's constantly telling me that something is wrong, and that I need to be worried. (takes a deep breath, trying to calm down) Sorry, it's just really hard for me to explain. It's like, my brain is just a constant whirlwind of worry and fear.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nods, eyes widening) Yes, that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, doing nothing, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. (takes a deep breath) It's like, my body is reacting to something, but my mind doesn't know what it is. I'll try to calm myself down, but it's hard. (pauses, looking anxious) Sometimes it happens when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Like, what if the baby gets hurt? What if I'm not a good enough mom? (shakes head) It's like, my brain just starts spiraling out of control, and I feel like I'm going to lose it. (looks down, voice cracking) And the worst part is, I feel like I'm losing control. Like, I'm not even in charge of my own body anymore. (pauses, taking a deep breath) It's scary, because I don't know what's causing it, and I don't know how to make it stop. (looks up, eyes welling up with tears) I just feel like I'm walking around, waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? Like, I'm just waiting for something to go wrong, and it's exhausting. (sighs) I just wish I could feel calm and peaceful again, like I used to before the baby was born.
Things have been getting on top of me

(nods, feeling a sense of relief that someone understands) Oh, yeah. That's exactly how I feel. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to deal with it all. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to be a good partner... it's just all so overwhelming. (sighs) And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be trying to make breakfast, and the baby will be crying, and I'll just feel like I'm at my breaking point. (shakes head) I'll think, "I just can't do this anymore. I'm just not capable of being a good mom." (looks down, feeling tears well up in her eyes) And then I'll feel guilty for feeling that way, because I know I'm supposed to be grateful for my baby, and I am grateful, but... (pauses, struggling to find the words) it's just hard, you know? It's hard to feel like I'm doing everything right, when it feels like everything is going wrong. (looks up, hoping for understanding) I just feel like I'm drowning in all of these responsibilities, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. (voice cracks) Sorry, I'm just really struggling right now.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nods, feeling a sense of recognition) Yes, that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because of the baby's schedule. I mean, the baby wakes up at night, of course, but even when the baby is sleeping, I'm still awake. (sighs) My mind just won't shut off, and I'll lie there thinking about all the things that are stressing me out. (pauses, looking down) And it's not just stress, it's sadness too. I'll feel this overwhelming sense of sadness, and I won't know how to make it go away. (looks up, eyes welling up with tears) I'll think about all the things I'm not doing right, all the things I'm failing at, and it just feels like this weight is crushing me. (pauses, taking a deep breath) And then, of course, there's the anxiety. I'll worry about the baby, about my relationship with my husband, about our future... (trails off, feeling overwhelmed) It's just, my mind is always racing, and I don't know how to calm it down. (looks up, hoping for help) I've tried to talk to my husband about it, but he just tells me to try to relax, to take some deep breaths. But it's not that easy. (shakes head) I feel like I'm losing myself in all of this, like I'm just disappearing into motherhood. (voice cracks) And it's scary, because I don't know how to find my way back.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nods, feeling a lump form in her throat) Yes, that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really feeling anything. I'm just numb, you know? (pauses, looking down) And then, out of nowhere, I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. It's like, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, or changing a diaper, and suddenly I'll just start crying. (shakes head) I don't even know why I'm crying, it's just... (trails off, feeling overwhelmed) It's like, everything is just too much for me, and I don't know how to handle it. (looks up, eyes welling up with tears) I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, you know? I'm supposed to be enjoying this time with my baby, but instead, I just feel sad and overwhelmed. (pauses, taking a deep breath) And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be trying to get the baby to sleep, and I'll just feel so frustrated and sad. (shakes head) I'll think, "Why can't I just get this right? Why can't I just be a good mom?" (looks down, feeling tears fall) And then, I'll just feel like I'm failing, like I'm not good enough. (voice cracks) It's just, being a mom is hard, and I don't know how to do it. (pauses, looking up) I feel like I'm just pretending to be a mom, like I'm just going through the motions, but I'm not really feeling anything. (shakes head) I don't know how to explain it, it's just... (trails off, feeling overwhelmed)
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nods, feeling a sense of relief that someone understands) Yes, that's been me a lot lately. I've been crying a lot, just feeling overwhelmed and sad. (pauses, looking down) It's like, I'll be doing something, and suddenly I'll just start crying. I'll be feeding the baby, or changing a diaper, and I'll just break down. (shakes head) I don't even know why I'm crying, it's just... (trails off, feeling emotional) It's like, everything is just too much for me, and I don't know how to handle it. (looks up, eyes welling up with tears) I'll cry about things that don't even make sense, like, I'll cry because the baby won't stop crying, or because I'm just so tired. (pauses, taking a deep breath) And then, I'll feel guilty for crying, because I'll think, "What's wrong with me? I'm a mom, I'm supposed to be strong." (shakes head) But it's hard, you know? It's hard to be strong when you're feeling so weak and overwhelmed. (looks down, feeling tears fall) I just wish I could be happy, you know? I wish I could just enjoy this time with my baby, without feeling so sad and anxious all the time. (pauses, looking up) But it's hard, because it feels like everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to cope. (voice cracks) I just feel like I'm losing myself, like I'm disappearing into motherhood. (starts to cry) I'm just so tired of feeling this way, I'm just so tired of being sad and overwhelmed all the time.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pauses, looking down, and speaking in a barely audible whisper) Yes... it has. (pauses again, collecting her thoughts) I don't know why, but sometimes I just feel so overwhelmed and hopeless, like I don't know how to keep going. (looks up, tears streaming down her face) And in those moments, I've thought about... about not being here anymore. (pauses again, struggling to find the words) It's not that I want to hurt myself, it's just that I feel like I'm drowning, and I don't know how to stay afloat. (looks down, feeling a wave of shame and guilt) I know it sounds crazy, but it's just... sometimes it feels like the only way to escape all the pain and sadness. (pauses, taking a deep breath) But I don't think I could ever actually do it. I have my baby to think about, and my husband... (trails off, feeling a sense of responsibility) I just feel like I'm stuck in this never-ending cycle of sadness and anxiety, and I don't know how to get out. (looks up, pleading for help) Please, you have to help me. I don't know what's wrong with me, but I know I need help. I just want to be a good mom, and a good person, but I feel like I'm failing at everything. (begins to sob) I just feel so lost and alone...
